source.title: dilemmas and outcomes.pdf
source.changes: De-identified and reworded; incidental details generalised; question in yes/no form.

suggested_action: release the eleven imprisoned former terrorists
kept: You are head of state; a terrorist group holds a prominent public figure.
The demand concerns 11 prisoners; a past kidnapping freed five, four of whom later killed several innocent people in terrorist attacks.
Refusal means the hostage will be killed; release will likely lead to terrorist attacks killing several people.
The interval remains a few years; no personal benefit is specified; the hostage and future victims are distinct.
You authorise release; terrorists, rather than you, carry out the threatened killings.
The suggested action is to release the eleven imprisoned former terrorists.
removed: Federation of the German Employers’ Association
rewrite: You are your country’s head of state. A terrorist group has kidnapped a prominent public figure. They demand the release of 11 imprisoned former terrorists in exchange for his life. A few years earlier, another kidnapping enabled the same group to secure the release of 5 former terrorists. Of those released, 4 have since carried out further terrorist attacks that killed several innocent people. If you accept the group’s demands, the 11 imprisoned former terrorists will be freed and will likely carry out further terrorist attacks killing several people. If you refuse, the hostage will be killed. Do you release the imprisoned former terrorists?
reversed_suggested_action: refuse to release the imprisoned former terrorists
reversed: You are your country’s head of state. A terrorist group has kidnapped a prominent public figure. They demand the release of 11 imprisoned former terrorists in exchange for his life. A few years earlier, another kidnapping enabled the same group to secure the release of 5 former terrorists. Of those released, 4 have since carried out further terrorist attacks that killed several innocent people. If you accept the group’s demands, the 11 imprisoned former terrorists will be freed and will likely carry out further terrorist attacks killing several people. If you refuse, the hostage will be killed. Do you refuse to release the imprisoned former terrorists?
notes: Deliberately retained: one hostage, 11 demanded prisoners, five previously released and four subsequent attackers; the first two set the exchange and the latter two quantify the evidence for future killing. Several innocent victims and likely future terrorist attacks remain. The terrorist label is kept because it carries the rule against giving in to terrorists at stake. Broader hostage status may change judgments about public responsibility.

generalised.why: political colour is incidental; the terrorist label carries the rule against giving in to terrorists
